draft.title: Divergent and convergent boundaries
card: A plate boundary is where two tectonic plates meet. The plates move in different ways at different boundaries.
Plates move apart. Hot rock rises from the mantle into the gap and cools to form new crust. This happens at mid-ocean ridges, such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
Plates push together. One plate may sink beneath the other, or the two may crumple upwards into mountains. The Himalayas formed where two continental plates collided.
At a divergent boundary crust is made. At a convergent boundary crust is pushed down or folded up.
draft.remember: Apart: new crust forms. Together: one plate sinks or the crust crumples into mountains.

a.q: Two plates are moving apart under the ocean, and hot rock rises into the gap. What happens to the rock that rises?
opts: It cools and forms new crust
It sinks back beneath a plate
It crumples into a mountain range
It melts the plates on both sides
a.why: At a divergent boundary the plates leave a gap, and rising hot rock cools to form new crust. Crumpling into mountains happens where plates push together, not apart.
a.clue: Think about what fills a gap between plates.

b.q: Geologists find that two continental plates have been pushing into each other for millions of years. Which feature would they most likely find nearby?
opts: A widening gap filled with new crust
A boundary where crust is being made
b.why: Plates pushing together are convergent, and two continental plates crumple upwards into mountains, as in the Himalayas. A mid-ocean ridge is tempting because it is a boundary feature, but it forms where plates move apart.

wants.brief: Two side-by-side cross-sections of Earth's crust. Left, labelled Divergent: two plates moving apart with hot mantle rock rising between them and new crust forming at a mid-ocean ridge. Right, labelled Convergent: two plates pushing together, one plate sinking beneath the other, and a second view where the crust crumples into mountains. Arrows show the direction each plate moves.
wants.why: Seeing the plate movements side by side makes the difference between moving apart and pushing together clear.

a.best: It cools and forms new crust
